checks.title: One Wikidata item on more than one building
checks.method: Group registry buildings by their Wikidata item.
checks.rule: One item to one outline. An OSM wikidata tag outranks containment of the item coordinate; when an item names a complex (tower over a mall), attach it to the tower outline and list the podium as a separate building.

checks.title: Same occupant recorded twice in one building
checks.method: Within each building, occupants whose normalised names are equal (case, punctuation, "(n)" branch numbers, "Ltd", "the" removed). Split by whether the two records come from different sources (not merged) or the same source (mapped twice).
checks.rule: Merge on normalised name within one building, keeping every source record as provenance under one occupant id; same-source pairs need a human or a second key (FSA id, OSM id) before merging.

examples.name: Canary Wall | Canary Wall | Canary Wall
Poplar Wines and Spirits | Poplar Wines and Spirits

checks.title: Building named after an occupant or owner
checks.method: OSM name of the outline equals (after normalisation) the name or brand of an occupant, or the owner. Medium when Wikidata names the building differently or the building has several occupants; low for a single-use building (a pub, a hotel), where the name may be right.
checks.rule: Keep building name and occupant name as separate attributes. Building name precedence: Wikidata label, then OSM name unless it matches an occupant or brand, then address.

examples.osm_name: Point A Hotel London Canary Wharf

checks.title: Item and outline describe different things (granularity)
checks.method: Wikidata height is more than twice the measured height of the outline it is attached to (LiDAR or OSM): the item is a tower, the outline a podium or a part.
checks.rule: Model buildings as a hierarchy (complex, building, part) with each source attached at its own level; do not copy tower attributes onto a podium.

checks.title: Named OSM occupant outside every building outline
checks.method: Named OSM shops, offices, amenities, leisure, healthcare, tourism and craft features in the box that the registry did not place in or within 12 m of an outline.
checks.rule: Keep as unplaced occupants with their own position; attach to a building only through a second key (address, postcode with one building, mall).

checks.title: Occupant placed by proximity, not containment
checks.method: Occupants with placed = "near" (point outside the outline but within 12 m), against all placed occupants.
checks.rule: Store placement method and distance with each link; treat proximity links as lower confidence in joins.

checks.title: FSA position is the postcode centre, or shared by several premises
checks.method: FSA premises in E14 with a position: within 3 m of the ONSPD point for their own postcode, or at exactly the same coordinate as two or more other premises.
checks.rule: Give each position a precision class (surveyed point, address point, postcode centroid). A postcode-centroid position may place an occupant in a postcode, never in a building.

examples.name: AA Psychiatry
examples.why: 0 m from the postcode centre; 4 premises at one point

checks.title: Same branch placed far apart by two sources
checks.method: Branches matched to both an OSM feature and an FSA record that both have positions: distance between them.
checks.rule: Prefer the OSM position for placement (mapped on site) and keep the FSA id as an attribute; above 50 m, re-check the match itself.

checks.title: Postcode far from the feature that carries it
checks.method: OSM features with addr:postcode and FSA premises with a position: distance to the ONSPD point of that postcode. Flagged above 300 m.
checks.rule: A postcode is a delivery attribute, not a location. Use it to find candidates, then confirm with geometry; large-user and estate postcodes cover many buildings.

checks.title: Mall or below-ground occupant placed by a 2D footprint
checks.method: Occupants in a mall (CWG) or below ground (OSM level under 0, or a CWG "Mall Level -1"/"Lower Mall" level) that the registry placed in an outline which is not that mall and has no recorded floor below ground. The Canary Wharf malls run under several building footprints, so a point-in-outline test assigns their shops to whichever building is above.
checks.rule: Place mall and below-ground occupants in the mall (a 3D volume or a named complex) by its own key (CWG mall, OSM indoor and level), not by the 2D outline above them; keep the footprint building only as "above".

checks.title: Building heights disagree between sources
checks.method: Pairs of OSM height tag, Wikidata height and LiDAR height (only where the 3D model took the height from LiDAR) that differ by more than 10 m and 10%. ID-4 cases (granularity) are left out.
checks.rule: Keep every height with its source and date. For display: LiDAR for buildings older than the survey, the OSM tag or Wikidata for newer ones, and flag any pair beyond the tolerance.

checks.title: Floor counts disagree, or do not fit the height
checks.method: OSM building:levels against Wikidata floors above ground (difference of 2 or more); and height divided by floors outside 2.5 to 6 m.
checks.rule: Floors and height are separate attributes with their own sources; derive storey height only where both come from one source, and mark plausibility failures instead of correcting them.

checks.title: OSM level and Canary Wharf Group mall level disagree
checks.method: Occupants with both an OSM level tag and a CWG level ("Mall Level -1", "Street Level 0"): the offset CWG minus OSM, per mall.
checks.rule: Levels are labels in a building-specific scheme, not heights. Keep each source's label; map between schemes with a per-mall offset table measured from matched occupants; convert to m OD only through published slab levels.

checks.title: Category schemes do not line up (crosswalk)
checks.method: For branches found in both OSM and the FSA file: pairs of OSM tag and FSA business type, with counts. Not errors in themselves; pairs that cross families (shop against restaurant) are flagged.
checks.rule: Map every source category to one project vocabulary with a maintained crosswalk table; keep the source category as provenance.

checks.title: Station and tunnel levels from different sources disagree
checks.method: Published levels in data/sourced-levels.json grouped by station and line. A depth below ground is turned into m OD with the LiDAR ground at the station node (docklands/data/area.js). Pairs more than 2 m apart are flagged; the control marked superseded_by is the one not applied.
checks.rule: A level against a stated datum from the asset owner (TfL rail levels, Crossrail slab levels) outranks a rounded depth from a secondary source. Keep the others as evidence, never average them. A depth "below ground" needs its reference point (street, ticket hall, ground outside the station) before it can be compared.

checks.title: Repeated word in an address
checks.method: Source address strings (FSA, CWG) with an address word twice in a row ("Unit Unit", "London London"), after the business name is removed from the front of the address (FSA addresses often start with it, and names such as "Tian Tian" repeat on purpose).
checks.rule: Normalise addresses into fields (unit, number, building, street, postcode) before matching; never match on the raw string.

checks.title: Level values our parser cannot read
checks.method: OSM level tags in the box, read by tools/osm-values.mjs osmLevels (lists with ";" or ",", ranges such as "0-2", fractions such as "0.5"). Issues: tokens it cannot read ("G", "roof"). The breakdown counts the readable values that are not a single whole number.
checks.rule: Parse levels into a list with the raw value kept; a ranged occupant spans floors, a fractional one is a mezzanine; an unreadable token needs a per-building table, not a guess.

checks.title: Postcodes that are malformed, never allocated or terminated
checks.method: Every postcode on an OSM feature or an FSA premises (OSM lists of several postcodes split on ";"), checked against the UK format and, inside E14, the ONSPD (August 2026). Postcodes outside E14 are checked for format only.
checks.rule: Validate postcodes on ingest against the current ONSPD; keep a terminated postcode as history with its end date, never as a current address.

checks.title: Wikidata numbers with extra tokens
checks.method: Numeric Wikidata facts in the registry (height, floors) whose stored value is not a single number ("33 1": two statements joined).
checks.rule: Fetch quantity statements with rank and qualifiers; keep the preferred-rank value and list the others.

checks.title: OSM multi-value tags read as one value by our tools
checks.method: OSM separates several values with ";" ("E14 9DT;E14 9FQ"). For every OSM feature in the box whose addr:postcode is a list: is each postcode of the list in the registry record that holds the feature (the building itself, or the building it is an occupant of)? A postcode missing there is a link our tools lost. The breakdown counts list values per tag in the source (not errors in themselves).
checks.rule: Split ";" lists on ingest for every tag (tools/osm-values.mjs osmList), keep the order, and test the parsers on multi-value fixtures.

checks.title: Branch addresses with "Unit Unit"
checks.method: registry/sources/brands/tools/build-branches.mjs writes "Unit " before OSM addr:unit, and mappers often put "Unit 14" (not "14") in addr:unit. Counted: OSM addr:unit values that already start with "Unit", and branch addresses that carry the doubled word.
checks.rule: Parse unit designators ("Unit", "Kiosk", "Stand") out of the value before formatting; never prefix a label to a free-text field.

checks.title: Parts of the walking network not joined to the rest
checks.method: Connected parts of the OSM walking network in the Canary Wharf area after joining stairs, escalators, lifts and walkable areas; points and named places outside the largest part.
checks.rule: Route only within one connected part; report places that cannot be reached; feed the gaps to mappers or close them from estate plans.

checks.title: Two levels joined at one point with no stairs, lift or ramp
checks.method: OSM nodes shared by ways tagged with different levels where no stair, escalator or lift way meets. Often a podium mapped as level 1 meeting a street at level 0, or an unmapped ramp or escalator.
checks.rule: Keep the join for routing but label it "level change not mapped"; settle each case from estate plans: a ramp, a missing connector, or a level-scheme difference (the estate podium against street level).

checks.title: Escalators and lifts without their levels
checks.method: Escalator ways with no level tag (drawn on level 0, so they change no level), lifts with fewer than two levels, and stairs or escalators whose ends could not be oriented.
checks.rule: A connector must state the levels it joins (level=-1;0) and its direction; add the missing tags from station and mall plans.

checks.title: Places with no mapped corridor on their own level
checks.method: Named shops, food and drink, services and platforms attached to the network on a different level from their own, because no path on their level lies within 40 m.
checks.rule: Map the mall corridors per level (indoor=corridor with level), or attach the place to its mall level from the estate plan; mark such routes as approximate.

checks.title: TfL and OSM number station levels differently
checks.method: Each TfL step-free station point (GTFS pathways, level index counted from the street) against the level of the nearest OSM network point within 35 m. Pairs that differ show where the two schemes disagree or where OSM lacks the level (the Elizabeth line platforms at Canary Wharf are TfL -4, but the nearest OSM points are at 0).
checks.rule: Keep each scheme; join TfL and OSM only at street level; build a per-station level table from published levels (m OD) before mixing schemes.

checks.title: Food hygiene rating older than three years, or pending
checks.method: FSA premises in E14 with a rating date before 2023-10-03, or flagged as awaiting a new rating.
checks.rule: Carry the source date on every attribute; for display, age out ratings and say how old each is.

checks.title: Canary Wharf Group directory: age of the copies
checks.method: Age of each Internet Archive copy used, and of the sitemap date of the page.
checks.rule: Treat directory facts as dated observations (observed_on = archive date); re-crawl before use, and expire entries not seen in the latest crawl.
checks.count_only: entries with a copy older than 180 days

checks.title: Companies registered here that are not active
checks.method: Company status other than "Active" at Canary Wharf postcodes (liquidation, proposal to strike off, administration and others).
checks.rule: Keep status and its date; exclude non-active companies from "who is here" views but keep them for history.

checks.title: Wikidata occupants and headquarters without dates, or former
checks.method: Occupant (P466) and headquarters (P159) links used in the registry, against their P580 start and P582 end qualifiers and the organisation's P576 dissolution, fetched in one QLever query by tools/build-categories.mjs (data/raw/registry/wikidata-occupant-classes.json). Former: an end date or a dissolved organisation, still listed as an occupant by the registry. Undated: no qualifier, so a former tenant cannot be told from a current one.
checks.rule: Carry the link status (current, former, undated) with every Wikidata occupant; never show a former occupant as current; treat undated links as "at some time".

checks.title: Fields filled, by entity type
checks.method: Share of registry buildings and occupants with each attribute.
checks.rule: Report fill rates with every composite layer; a missing value is "unknown", not zero.

checks.title: Which sources see each branch or directory entry
checks.method: Source combinations for the 271 chain-store branches, and the CWG directory entries that no other source has.
checks.rule: No single source is complete: a composite occupant layer needs every source, a match key per pair, and a record of which sources saw each occupant and when.

checks.title: Registered offices concentrated at one address
checks.method: Postcodes with 100 or more registered companies, and residential buildings with 20 or more. A registered office is a legal address: formation agents, accountants and serviced offices hold thousands.
checks.rule: Never read a registered office as an occupant. Composite "who works here" from occupancy sources (OSM, FSA, CWG, business rates when licensed); join Companies House only for identity and status.

checks.title: Positions that mean "kept here", not "found here"
checks.method: Heritage records whose coordinate is the holding museum (Wikidata P276) or a 1 km place box (Portable Antiquities Scheme), against all heritage records with a position.
checks.rule: Every position needs a relation type (site, find spot, holding place, centroid) and a precision; map layers filter on it.
checks.count_only: records; no issue record per heritage item
